drafted_from: tool row in tools/start-a-computer/tool-rows.json, do-work/check-a-sign-up.mjs and tools/start-a-computer/test/start-a-computer.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Prove https://front.example takes a new account end to end: sign up, sign in and read a signed-in page."
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it takes one https origin, makes one synthetic account with a one-run software passkey and answers each step's status.
instructions: 1. Pick the origin: https://host with no path (a path is refused).

2. Say the line in start_here. Your AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: "tool:check-a-sign-up"} and runs node tools/start-a-computer/do-work/check-a-sign-up.mjs https://front.example. No credential is needed.
3. Read the JSON line: origin, address, steps and signed_in_read. Exit code 1 when signed_in_read is false; name the step that stopped.
4. Each run leaves one synthetic account at the computer that took it: call it synthetic wherever accounts are counted.

worked_examples.title: A passing check: seven steps, a new address, a signed-in read
worked_examples.ask: Does the sign-up at front.example work end to end?
worked_examples.given: From tools/start-a-computer/test/start-a-computer.test.mjs ('the sign-up check answers the way a browser does and its passkey signs what it says'). Run: node tools/start-a-computer/do-work/check-a-sign-up.mjs https://front.example
